title: Paying a Member's Equity Back Out Under the Board's Revolvement Cycle for One Allocation Year
content:
Equity comes back to the member on the board's cycle, and what a year's revolvement pays under Membership and Patronage Equity is worked out from the equity account itself rather than from any figure printed on a statement. The pool the board fixes acts on the credits the fiscal year drawn on carries rather than on the whole of the equity standing unrevolved.

The observable effect is a revolvement line on the member's equity account against the allocation year named, dated today, and the member's equity falls by the amount paid. No allocation is declared and no membership standing changes. The member sees the revolvement as a payment line on the equity statement and receives the money on the cooperative's ordinary remittance run.

## Making the entry

The entry is made with the agent-side tool `record_equity_revolvement_d16ad296`, which is unlocked and then called by the agent. One call adds one revolvement line.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `membership_id` | the internal reference number of the equity membership the revolvement is paid on | an identifier, as returned by the equity membership lookup |
| `fiscal_year` | the allocation year whose equity is being revolved | a four-digit fiscal year, such as 2026; the fiscal year ends 31 August and is named for the calendar year in which it ends, and there is no empty value |
| `revolvement_amount` | the equity paid back out to the member on this line | USD to 2 decimal places, half a cent rounding up, never negative |

## What comes back

A single confirmation sentence naming the equity ledger reference minted for the revolvement line, the amount paid back out and the allocation year it was drawn from. The sentence appearing at all is what indicates the revolvement was written; a failure raises instead of returning.
